ai.description: *Raorchestes chlorosomma* is a small bushfrog (25–30 mm) with a brownish-green dorsum and distinctive emerald-green irises. It is identified by its granular skin and lack of webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes chlorosomma* is uniquely distinguished from similar bushfrogs by its distinct, vibrant emerald-green iris, which contrasts sharply with its brownish body.
ai.habitat: The Green-eyed Bushfrog inhabits the canopy and understory of evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically at altitudes between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Green-eyed Bushfrog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among foliage during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes chlorosomma* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes chlorosomma* is endemic to the Munnar landscape in the Western Ghats of Kerala, India, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Raorchestes chlorosomma* emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from the dense canopy of high-altitude evergreen forests.
